Hi Sara / Ops team,

Thanks again for the time last week — really excited to get EdgeHealth into a short POC so we can validate prompt behavior, routing profiles, and run a couple of controlled load tests. To make the hands-on session productive, would you be able to share which environment you want first: a short Hosted trial (fast to spin up) or a short Dedicated reservation (better for steady QPS)? Our typical POC flow is:

- 60–90 minute kickoff + prompt review (team walks through 5–7 canonical prompts)
- 90 minute hands-on lab (routing configuration, KV/prefix cache checks, and a sand-boxed load test ramp)
- 30 minute capacity recap and next steps (quota bump requests, token budget recommendations)

Quick asks for planning:
- Preferred dates/times next week (we’re flexible morning PT or late-morning ET)
- Estimated peak QPS you expect during your real workload (even a range helps us choose Dedicated vs Hosted)
- Any security observers to include on the session?

I’ve attached a draft agenda and an initial capacity estimate (token assumptions and rate-limit suggestions). We can run the load test on Hosted for short bursts (up to ~200 RPS sustained for 10–15 minutes) but for longer sustained runs we recommend Dedicated reserve.

Propose two options to save back-and-forth:
- Wed, Nov 16, 09:30–12:00 PT (kickoff + lab)
- Fri, Nov 18, 11:00–13:30 PT (kickoff + lab)

If those don’t work, send me two slots and we’ll adapt.

Best,
Naomi Feldman

Marcus / Avery — forwarding EdgeHealth’s constraints and the ask to run both Hosted and Dedicated flows during the Nov 18 session. Key points and proposal below so we can move quickly: 

EdgeHealth POC targets (from Sara):
- Short burst: 150–180 RPS, 95th token length ~320 tokens (30–45 minute window)
- Sustained: ~120 RPS for ~2 hours

Proposal (what we need to prepare):
1) Hosted burst plan (Avery):
   - Temporary quota bump to support burst to 180 RPS for 30 minutes. Recommend rate-limit profile: 350 requests/min per token-key with 5s concurrency window and aggressive batching.
   - Preconfigure a sample routing policy that falls back to a cheaper open model if latency spikes. Demo will show latency/price tradeoff.

2) Dedicated trial (Marcus):
   - Provision a short Dedicated pool for Friday Nov 18 afternoon (target window: provision by Nov 16 EOD to allow testing).
   - Suggested reservation: 2 x medium GPU nodes (estimate in capacity_estimate_v2.xlsx) — gives headroom to sustain 120 RPS at the token sizes noted.
   - Prepare IP allowlist doc and a short certificate exchange checklist for EdgeHealth SRE.

3) Load test choreography (Naomi):
   - Run Hosted burst first (10m warmup, 30m peak), then switch traffic to Dedicated for 90–120m steady window.
   - Need EdgeHealth to provide load agents and endpoint list; Ops can run from their VPC or we can run from our load farm.

Marcus — can you confirm:
- Provision time if we submit a request today (aim Nov 16 finish)?
- Any quota or billing approvals needed for a short Dedicated trial?

Avery — I’ll hand off the routing demo notes and the two example prompt sets (attached). Can you prepare the fallback model switch demo and a short script to show token usage breakdown in the console?

Thanks team — I’ll draft the calendar invite and the load test plan once I hear back.
